summary: The Republic of Indonesia, independent from the Netherlands after 1945, invaded Portuguese Timor in December 1975, months after Portugal's administration collapsed there, and annexed it the following year. It occupied the territory until 1999, when it accepted a United Nations ballot on autonomy; the vote went against it, and its withdrawal was preceded by militia violence that destroyed much of the territory. Only a handful of states recognised the annexation, and Portugal never did. It is in the atlas as the actor that took the last territory Portugal had failed to decolonise.
